q: How do you tell one story to four different rooms?
form: Four rooms, and the one thing only each of them saw
subject: What each deck has that the other three do not
rows: Early investors
The people. They knew the founders.
The company's own words, large: “Original Resolute Intimate Fearless Ready”
Values-driven investors
The world they want to put money behind.
People photographed the way they would want to be seen
Angels who have run companies
The engine.
Four numbers, each beside the one it beats
Syndicates
What is exceptional.
Invitations to customers' weddings
end: Take those four slides away and the four decks are one company's same facts.
close: We find what each room came for, and put that part of the truth first.
from: The work deck; the four things are Kahran's own (connection, values, unit economics, the opportunity), from his talk of August 2025

q: How do you change the story without changing the facts?
form: The same fact, on two slides
subject: One fact at a time, as it was drawn for one room and then for another
rows: A generation is changing who buys
A photograph and a line: “Why tomboyx is the Brand of the Future”
A bar for each generation: “A Generational Shift in Identity”
The old market leader is fading
One sentence in a paragraph
Its own column, in numbers: “Dwindling former leader”
The company's numbers are very good
One line of them, under the people
Four dials, each with the market beside it: “Best in class premium basics KPIs”
end: For one room the people are told around the numbers. For the other the numbers are told around the people. Neither has a fact the other lacks.
close: We keep the facts fixed and move everything else.
frames: The same fact, for the angels
The old leader, as a column
from: The real slides; the last line is Kahran's way of putting it, in my words

q: How do you make someone feel a company before they fund it?
subject: What the eye meets first, second and third in the deck for the values-driven investors
rows: First, a person
Photographed the way they would want to be seen: “Imagery nods to the female gaze in a deliberate repudiation of male gaze focused marketing.”
Whether this is their kind of company
Then, the company speaking
Its own words, unsoftened, signed off “Fit for You.”
Whether it means it
Only then, the market
The size of it, and who else has been funded
Whether it is also a good investment
end: By the time the numbers arrive they are proof of something already felt.
close: We choose what is seen first for the person doing the seeing.
from: The work deck's page on the values-driven investors, and the real slides

q: How do you pitch when you are not in the room?
form: Before the call, and on it
subject: The deck for the syndicates, which is read by a screener before anyone gets to speak
heads: On the call: with the leaders there
rows: Who is there
Someone screening, who will not decide
The people who decide, and the people who run the company
What has to work
The titles. Read only those and the pitch is still there: “Key highlights”, “Honored to have an extended family”, “Run by a strong team”
The team, in person
What it is for
“getting the company past screening rounds and in front of decision makers”
“bringing key leadership to be part of the pitch”
end: The deck's job is to earn the call. The call is where the pitch happens.
close: We design for the reader the deck reaches after you have left.
from: The work deck's page on the syndicates

q: How do you turn being loved into a reason to invest?
form: One slide, put in the deck where nobody expected it
subject: A single slide: the invitations customers send the company
rows: The slide
“Honored to have an extended family”: invitations to weddings and graduations, posted to the office by customers.
Where you would expect it
In the deck for the people who already love the company.
Where it went
In the deck for the investors who came for a good company at a low price.
Why there
They value a company by its numbers. This is the one thing the numbers do not show, so it is shown to the people who would never go looking for it.
end: Love stops being a nice ending and becomes part of what is being bought.
close: We treat affection as data, and show it like data.
from: Kahran's talk of August 2025 says which deck it went into and why, in my words; the slide is real

q: How do you know a story is working?
form: A round that fills, room by room
subject: The raise itself, in the order the rooms were asked
heads: What the story had to do
rows: First: the early investors
Honour what they already felt, and blame no one
A little. The hardest ask of the four.
Second: the values-driven
Let them see they were among their own
About half
Third: the angels
Make an unfamiliar business readable
Most of it
Fourth: the syndicates
Get past the screening
Full
end: Each version was written because the round was not yet full. The measure of each is what the next room started with.
close: We judge a story by what happens after it is told.
from: The order and how full the round was after each are from Kahran's talk of August 2025, in my words; no amounts are given here
